title: Fire radiative power and energy
text: FRP is instantaneous fire radiative power in MW, equivalent to MJ per second. FRE is energy integrated over time in MJ. One GJ is 1000 MJ. Summing instantaneous satellite FRP samples does not give energy. The local scientific energy tool integrates calibrated daily FRE over the cube cells represented each day. Estimates depend on temporal reconstruction and sensor coverage.

title: Satellite detections and incident identity
text: NASA FIRMS detections are satellite thermal anomalies, not a count of distinct fires. A single fire may generate many detections over different sensors and days. Thermal anomalies can also be agricultural burning or industrial sources. A selected polygon or H3 hexagon is a query area, not a confirmed wildfire perimeter. Zero detections do not prove absence of fire: clouds, overpasses, thresholds and archive coverage affect observation.

title: MODIS and VIIRS sensor comparability
text: VIIRS provides 375 m active-fire detection, while the nominal MODIS active-fire product is 1 km. Resolution, sensitivity and overpass differences can alter raw counts. Introducing VIIRS from 2012 is not proof of an increase in actual fire incidents. There is no universal 400 or 420 percent correction. The application uses calibrated FRE rather than raw counts for scientific energy comparisons.

title: Reconstruction and uncertainty
text: RTS Kalman smoothing estimates missing daily thermal measurements using a state model, other available sensors and a historical cross-sensor prior. A reconstructed value is an estimate, not a direct observation or proof of a continuing fire. A 95 percent model interval describes uncertainty of the modeled state; it is not the probability that a named fire occurred. Partially reconstructed days can also contain real observations.

title: Ignition and fire spread evidence
text: Satellite thermal detections alone cannot establish what ignited a fire. Ignition evidence requires a matching investigation or incident report. Wind, high temperature, low humidity and fuel conditions can affect spread but do not establish ignition. A command post location is not necessarily the location of a fire. A regional report is not proof that each selected satellite cell belongs to that incident. A cause absent from retrieved reports is unverified in those reports, not necessarily unknown to authorities.

title: Biomass and emission estimates
text: The application estimates dry biomass consumed using 0.368 kg per MJ of integrated FRE. For GJ this is energy_GJ times 0.368 tonnes. Episode scenario emissions assume 9.5 g PM2.5 per kg biomass and 1580 g CO2 per kg biomass. These constant factors do not establish measured emissions, ambient air concentrations, health impacts, casualties, ecological damage or burned hectares. Emission factors vary with fuel and combustion. Dashboard PM2.5 and burned-area validation fields can remain null.

title: Industrial thermal screening
text: Persistent thermal activity can indicate gas flaring or another industrial heat source. Temporal entropy or an industrial screening flag alone does not identify a facility. Current real-cube industrial scores may remove no cells; report actual counts rather than promising filter effectiveness. Industrial candidates should not automatically be explained using wildfire news.

title: Local archive and map scope
text: The scientific cube covers available Earth observations within 2001–2026; actual date coverage varies by area. Four UI study envelopes are Iberia (Spain and Portugal), Chilecito La Rioja Argentina, Orlando Florida USA, and Amazonas/Manaus Brazil. The Amazonas envelope is not all Amazonia. Selected polygons and dates take priority unless the current question explicitly changes place or time. H3 R7 cells and unique R4 parents filter the database. Scientific totals integrate the daily represented footprint, not the full polygon every day. Synthetic mode is opt-in and cannot verify real incidents.

title: Thermal episode duration
text: The episode profiling tool discovers the greatest daily energy within available history when no date is specified. It computes consecutive above-background activity in a window of 15 days before and after the peak, with robust same-month background from other years. This is a statistical thermal episode that can include several fires. It is not the official ignition, containment or extinction interval. If activity reaches the window or archive edge its duration is censored and may extend beyond the reported interval.

title: Visible map versus regional energy estimate
text: The visible map integrates calibrated observations per H3 cell and does not include regional Kalman reconstruction. The regional model first averages each sensor over potentially different sets of cells, then combines sensors and optionally reconstructs missing values. These are different estimators, so totals can differ even with reconstruction disabled. Compare the same area, inclusive dates and industrial settings. Biomass must use the matching energy: 0.368 tonnes per GJ. Observed cell footprint differs from selected polygon area; neither is measured burned area. A full-year selection can contain only the days available before the archive cutoff.

title: Fire season timing: peak burning date, season duration and decadal drift
text: The fire season tool summarises each complete calendar year by its peak burning date, the energy-weighted circular centre of that year's fire activity, and by its season duration in days, an effective seasonal width derived from how concentrated the activity is. Decadal drift is the Theil-Sen slope of the yearly peak dates in days per decade: positive means the peak arrives later, negative earlier. Its p-value is a rank test without correction for year-to-year correlation. A weakly seasonal year gives a long duration and an unstable peak. Partial years are excluded. This describes when satellites record fire energy, not when ignitions are permitted or likely.

title: Period comparison, percentage change and the internal calculator
text: Comparisons between two years, seasons or months are computed by the server from the same daily series as the dashboard: total energy, dry biomass consumed, mean daily energy and the highest single day for each period, with percentage change equal to second minus first, divided by first, times 100. A percentage change is undefined when the first period is zero. The language model never performs this arithmetic; each figure is shown with its formula as a verified calculation. A period that runs past the archive end is compared on its available days only, and differences in satellite coverage between periods can contribute to a change.

title: Thermal risk outlook and intensity regimes
text: The risk outlook reports the probability that satellites record high non-persistent heat or a persistent-source thermal excursion within 24 hours, 7 days and 14 days. It is a satellite thermal-event proxy, not a forecast of a confirmed ignition. The 24-hour figure is the sum of a seasonal baseline for that time of year, a multi-year shift comparing recent years with the long record, and a short-term surge from recent heat and activity in adjacent cells. Longer windows accumulate with day-to-day persistence instead of treating days as independent. Intensity regimes use per-detection radiative power: below 25 MW low surface intensity, 25 to 120 MW moderate surface fire, 120 to 350 MW high intensity, above 350 MW extreme. These bands are indicative and do not replace an on-site assessment.

title: Validated burned area from MCD64A1
text: Burned area in hectares comes only from the MCD64A1 500 m burned-area product, when its complete monthly tiles have been published locally for the area and year. It includes burned cells that have no active-fire detection, and it can miss small or low-intensity burns. Fire energy per burned hectare divides the model-derived energy of the same calendar years by that area. When MCD64A1 is not available the answer is unavailable: detection counts, radiative power and energy cannot be converted into hectares.

title: Historically quiet windows for planned burning
text: The quiet-window tool averages the daily fire energy density and the previous-day energy of adjacent cells for each calendar day across the full record, then ranks 30-day windows from the lowest values. It shows when satellites have historically recorded the least fire activity and the least spread between neighbouring cells in the selected area. It is not a burn authorisation or a weather forecast: fuel moisture, wind, staffing and local regulations decide whether a prescribed or agricultural burn is safe. Days without a detection count as quiet although cloud can hide activity.

title: Reconstructed days and stationary industrial heat
text: A reconstructed day is one where an evidenced sensor outage or cloud cover left no usable observation and the daily energy was estimated by smoothing. Days with no coverage evidence are left unfilled rather than assumed to be zero. Stationary industrial heat, such as gas flaring, is screened by year-round persistence and a match to published flare sites; vegetation fire is seasonal and moves. The data-quality tool reports how many cells carry the persistent-source flag and their share of all detections. The flag is a screening result: it does not name a facility, and an unflagged cell is not proof of vegetation fire.
